title: Now Hear This!
intro:
November 7–13, 2026. Theme: The Great Controversy Over the Voice of God: Why Humanity Resists Divine Revelation.

In earlier studies, we established that God communicates through prophets to reveal His character, restore His image in humanity, and maintain a saving relationship with fallen humanity. This week's lesson addresses the other side of that communication: Why do human beings resist the very messages God sends for their salvation?
heroQuote: The great controversy is fundamentally a conflict over whose word can be trusted and whose character will be reproduced in humanity.

footer.text: Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.

themes.title: I. Introduction: The Great Controversy Is a Conflict Over Whose Voice We Will Trust
themes.summary: Eden introduced a conflict over whether humanity would trust God's goodness or Satan's accusations. Prophetic messages continue God's work of restoring that trust and renewing His image in us.

themes.title: II. The First Response to Prophecy: Fear and Unbelief
themes.summary: Israel's fear turned into rebellion when visible dangers outweighed confidence in God's promises. Joshua and Caleb show how trust in His character changes our response to the same difficult circumstances.

themes.title: III. The Second Response: Rejecting the Message to Preserve Self-Rule
themes.summary: Jehoiakim burned Jeremiah's scroll to resist correction and preserve his own authority. His response illustrates how pride and cherished sin can lead people to reject warnings God sends out of compassion to invite repentance and forgiveness.

themes.title: IV. The Third Response: Honoring the Prophets While Rejecting Their Message
themes.summary: The Pharisees celebrated earlier prophets while resisting their message and rejecting Christ. Truly receiving prophecy means allowing it to lead us into a relationship with Jesus that changes our character.

themes.title: V. The Purpose of Prophetic Warnings: Restoring God's Image in Humanity
themes.summary: Paul uses Israel's failures to help believers recognize destructive desires, idolatry, and distrust in themselves. These warnings call us to humility and a character shaped by Christ, guarding against the assumption that we cannot fall.

themes.title: Different Manifestations of the Same Underlying Problem
themes.summary: Fear, pride, persistent resistance, hypocrisy, and complacency take different forms but share a common root: placing human preferences above God's revelation. These biblical examples invite us to examine how we respond when His word challenges us.

themes.title: Prophecy as an expression of the Circuit of Beneficence
themes.summary: Prophecy expresses God's self-giving love, inviting trust, repentance, and obedience that restore His image in us and inspire service to others. Rejecting His messages interrupts this circuit of beneficence by resisting the transforming love He continues to offer.

images.alt: Prophecy as an expression of the Circuit of Beneficence
images.caption: Circuit of Beneficence

themes.title: The connection to the final generation
themes.summary: The lesson connects Eden's deception with Revelation's final crisis: both turn on trust in God's character and word. Prophetic guidance prepares believers to recognize counterfeit authority and remain faithful as that trust is tested.
